title: Discrete-time quantum walks with energy-dependent coins
authors: Alana Spak dos Santos, Thiago T. Tsutsui, Fabiano M. Andrade
abstract: In this work, we extend the scattering quantum walk (SQW) framework to a lattice of energy-dependent point interactions. This yields, within the coined quantum walk (CQW) formalism, a coin operator that is directly related to the scattering matrix of zero-range potentials. The model thus provides a discrete-time quantum-walk (DTQW) analog of a periodic array of point interactions of the Kronig-Penney type, where the walker's wavenumber serves as a continuous, physically transparent control parameter for the coin operation. We analyze the spectra and the dynamics of position probability and entanglement, yielding distinct results for specific energies and point interactions. We relate the spectral structure to the spatial probability distribution and explicitly characterize the long-time entanglement behavior for each point interaction. The transmission modulus determines the quasienergy gap, bandwidth, and maximum group velocity, while also controlling the long-time coin-position entanglement for the initial state considered. The four families of one-dimensional point interactions ($δ$, $δ'$, crossed and asymmetric) realize qualitatively distinct transmission profiles and span the full range of behavior, including enhanced or strongly suppressed spreading and oscillatory entanglement.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical model for discrete-time quantum walks by mapping them onto a lattice of energy-dependent point interactions. By relating the coin operator to the scattering matrix, the authors show that the walk's spectral properties and entanglement dynamics are controlled by the transmission coefficient. This framework is valuable for understanding wave propagation in structured media.
main_problem: The work extends the scattering quantum walk (SQW) framework to model discrete-time quantum walks (DTQWs) on a lattice featuring energy-dependent point interactions.
main_result: The transmission modulus controls the quasienergy gap, bandwidth, and long-time coin-position entanglement, while different point interaction types yield distinct spreading and entanglement behaviors.
method: The analysis compares the Coined Quantum Walk (CQW) and Scattering Quantum Walk (SQW) formalisms, utilizing the scattering matrix derived from zero-range potentials to define an energy-dependent coin operator.
model_or_system: The model is a DTQW analog of a periodic array of point interactions, mathematically realized by relating the coin operator to the scattering matrix of zero-range potentials, allowing the walker's wavenumber to act as a continuous control parameter.
key_observables: Quasienergy spectrum, spatial probability distribution, and coin-position entanglement.
important_parameters: The walker's wavenumber (energy $k$), the transmission modulus $|t(k)|$, and the specific type of point interaction ($\delta, \delta', 	ext{crossed, asymmetric}$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are analyzed by assuming the scattering matrix $S(k)$ and coin operator $C_c(k)$ are uniform across all vertices at a fixed energy $k$.
figures_summary: Figures compare probability curves for SQW and CQW, show reflection/transmission probabilities vs. $k$ for four interaction types, and illustrate the time evolution of entanglement for these cases.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the equivalence between CQW and SQW, derives the energy-dependent coin operator from scattering theory, analyzes the spectral properties using the transmission modulus, and finally characterizes the long-time entanglement behavior for various point interactions.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, physically transparent link between wave scattering theory (Kronig-Penney type potentials) and the dynamics of quantum walks, offering tunable control over spectral gaps and entanglement via the energy parameter.
